20261103AZ84697.description: Arizona Proposition 141. Prohibits taxes and fees based on vehicle miles traveled.
20261103AZ84697.summary: This proposed amendment to Arizona's constitution would prohibit state and local governments from imposing taxes or fees based on vehicle miles traveled and bar them from monitoring vehicle miles traveled without consent.

20261103AZ84698.description: Arizona Proposition 316. Limits local sales taxes on food.
20261103AZ84698.summary: This ballot measure would cap local sales taxes on food at 2%, subject new or increased food sales taxes to voter approval, and prohibit them from taking effect before June 30, 2027.

20261103AZ84699.description: Arizona Proposition 317. Declares drug cartels to be terrorist organizations.
20261103AZ84699.summary: This ballot measure would declare that drug cartels are terrorist organizations and direct the Arizona Department of Homeland Security to address their threat.

20261103AZ84700.description: Arizona Proposition 144. Requires proof of identity to vote and prohibits noncitizens from voting.
20261103AZ84700.summary: This proposed amendment to Arizona's constitution would prohibit noncitizens from voting, require government-issued proof of identity to vote and bar foreign contributions and expenditures in elections.
20261103AZ84700.seatName: 144 - Require voter ID and citizenship to vote

20261103AZ84701.description: Arizona Proposition 142. Expands prohibition on preferential treatment based on race or ethnicity.
20261103AZ84701.summary: This proposed amendment to Arizona's constitution would expand prohibitions on preferential treatment based on race or ethnicity for state agencies and higher education institutions, including mandatory statements in support of race-based diversity, equity and inclusion efforts.
20261103AZ84701.seatName: 142 - Prohibit race-based preferential treatment or discrimination

20261103AZ84702.description: Arizona Proposition 319. Restricts use of traffic enforcement cameras.
20261103AZ84702.summary: This ballot measure would prohibit new contracts for camera license plate readers to enforce traffic laws starting in 2027 and require approval from local voters to continue existing arrangements.
20261103AZ84702.seatName: 319 - Prohibit traffic photo enforcement systems without voter approval

20261103AZ84712.description: Arizona Proposition 320. Requires large school districts to spend at least 60% on instruction.
20261103AZ84712.summary: This ballot measure would require school districts with at least 7,500 students or those located in counties with at least 500,000 residents to spend at least 60% of their operating costs on direct instructional expenses.

20261103AZ84713.description: Arizona Proposition 318. Expands restriction on transgender athletes in school sports.
20261103AZ84713.summary: This ballot measure would expand an existing prohibition on male athletes participating on female school sports teams, add restrictions on locker rooms and define a person's sex according to what was listed on an original birth certificate.
20261103AZ84713.seatName: 318 - Require school facility access based on sex assigned at birth

20261103AZ84970.description: Mesa Measure 1. Authorizes $150 million of bonds for public safety facilities and equipment.
20261103AZ84970.summary: This ballot measure would authorize Mesa to issue $150 million in general obligation bonds to fund fire, medical, police and other public safety facilities, equipment, technology and land acquisition.
20261103AZ84970.seatName: Mesa-1 - Public safety general obligation bond

20261103AZ84971.description: Mesa Measure 2. Authorizes $135 million of bonds for street and transportation improvements.
20261103AZ84971.summary: This ballot measure would authorize Mesa to issue $135 million in general obligation bonds to fund street improvements and reconstruction, streetlights, traffic signals, shared-use paths and related land acquisition.
20261103AZ84971.seatName: Mesa-2 - Transportation improvements general obligation bond

20261103AZ84972.description: Mesa Amendment 3. Requires council meetings and public notices to follow state law.
20261103AZ84972.summary: This proposed amendment to Mesa's charter would require that procedures for scheduling City Council meetings, giving public notice and holding executive sessions follow state law.
20261103AZ84972.seatName: Mesa-3 - Council meeting procedures and public notice charter amendment

20261103AZ84973.description: Mesa Amendment 4. Requires ordinances to be posted online and published under state law.
20261103AZ84973.summary: This proposed amendment to Mesa's charter would require ordinances to be posted on the city's website and at one physical location in Mesa, and to be published in accordance with state law.
20261103AZ84973.seatName: Mesa-4 - Ordinance publication requirements charter amendment
